newsitem.title: USA: DEC shareholders to ponder low share price.
newsitem.headline: DEC shareholders to ponder low share price.

text.p: Institutional shareholders of Digital Equipment Corp meeting in New York next month will seek answers to explain the stock's performance, the organizer of the gathering said.
Digital shares, trading at 34-3/8 in late morning today, down 1/4, dipped as low as 25 earlier this year.

Herbert Denton, head of the broker-dealer Providence Capital Inc, who holds only a tiny amount of Digital stock, said he expected the owners of from 30 percent to 40 percent of Digital's outstanding stock to attend the June 18 meeting.

"If Compaq thinks DEC is worth $60, and you look at the breakup value of DEC in the high $60s...you say hey, you know, the issues facing this company need to be understood by the institutional investment community," Denton said.

The Wall Street Journal reported earlier this month that Compaq Computer Corp reached a general agreement to buy Digital for between $9 billion and $10 billion in 1995 but Digital backed away from the deal. Digital's shares have fallen in value since.

A spokesman for Digital did not return phone calls from Reuters seeking comment. But Digital spokesman Dan Kaferle told the Boston Globe, which first reported the gathering, that the company is striving to improve performance.
"We're not satisfied with our performance," Kaferle told the Globe. "We know we can do a lot better, and we are going to do a lot better."
Denton said the New York meeting will serve as an information session to discuss challenges facing Digital. He declined to say if any of the institutional shareholders had an agenda to pursue.

"Normally, when we've gotten to a point like this, we've got a very good idea of what strategic changes the major shareholders would be interested in," he said. "In the case of Digital, there are a lot of major issues facing the company that are not so clear cut."
Denton said he invited Digital Chief Executive Robert Palmer to address the meeting and report on the company's progress, but he declined.

"Mr. Palmer has been in the saddle now for five years or so, 57,000 people have lost their jobs, so there's been radical change and the level of profitability at this time is not that strong," Denton told Reuters in an interview.

The institutional shareholders are also interested in the promotion of Bruce Claflin to vice president of worldwide sales and marketing, he said. Shareholders are wondering if Claflin has enough power within the company to change Digital's culture from a focus on engineering to more toward sales and marketing, he said.
He said seven panelists, including mainframe designers, intellectual property rights experts and Wall Street analysts who have covered the company for many years will address the meeting.
The Boston Globe reported Thursday that Denton has taken on management at other companies before, including California Microwave Inc and Ashland Inc and is in a current battle with Comsat Corp.
